text.p: France, which long backed Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko and has much to fear from his replacement by rebel leader Laurent Kabila, on Sunday welcomed talks between the two men to find a peaceful settlement.

"France notes with satisfaction that this first contact allowed serious discussions to start which one hopes will lead to a solution in accordance with U.N. Security Council resolution 1097...," a French foreign ministry statement said.

"France recalls its attachment to an orderly transition which should lead to a democratic process. We hope the talks will resume quickly and that an effective cease-fire will take place," the statement said.
Resolution 1097 called for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Zaire.
Paris has long said Kabila was backed by neighbouring states but that issue was apparently not a major topic of discussion when Mobutu and Kabila met off the Congolese coast on Sunday.
France, as well as the United States, former colonial power Belgium and Britain, have troops across the Zaire River in Congo to evacuate their nationals from Kinshasa if need be.
